AIBD-0008.h: Crash warnings and automatic braking cut rear-end crash rates up to 50%
AIBD-0008.conf: found by a court or regulator
AIBD-0008.cmp: the same vehicle models where the optional systems were not purchased (and comparable luxury vehicles without standard low-speed AEB)
AIBD-0008.before: the same models where the optional systems were not purchased
AIBD-0008.after: reduced rear-end striking crash involvement rates by 27%, 43%, and 50%, respectively
AIBD-0008.later: Litigated on 17 January 2025: NHTSA adopted FMVSS No. 127 on 9 May 2024 after citing this study in its proposed rule. The rule requires AEB on new light vehicles from 1 September 2029. Auto Innovators asked the D.C. Circuit to review the rule on 17 January 2025, and the case has been in abeyance since February 2025. On 23 March 2026 the Department of Transportation told the court that it is preparing a proposal to amend the rule. The National Law Review reports that the proposal would extend the compliance lead time by two years.
AIBD-0008.sum: In an Insurance Institute for Highway Safety study, forward collision warning alone, low-speed emergency braking and warning with braking cut rear-end striking crash rates by 27%, 43% and 50%.
AIBD-0008.cb: Sources: two independent regulatory documents, one independent peer-reviewed study and one other independent source.

AIBD-0190.h: Chicago's model would have found food violations 7.5 days earlier

AIBD-0190.later: Challenged on 10 October 2019: The Department of Public Health began using the model in January 2015. AIBD-0190.sum: In a double-blind retrodiction of 1,637 Chicago food inspections from 2014, the city's Food Inspection Forecasting model would have found critical violations on average 7.5 days earlier.
AIBD-0190.cb: Sources: one independent news report, one independent preprint and the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
